workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§260–264
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§260–264: The sons’ rebuke and the western campaigns
part: §§260–264 — The sons’ rebuke and the western campaigns
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§260–264, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: The Sartaul campaign continues. Chinggis rebukes his three sons for keeping Ürüngechi to themselves, is calmed by his quiver-bearers, and sends Sormaqan against the Baqtad; Dorbai-Doqshin is sent against the city of Abtu and Sübegetei against peoples to the north; Jalawachi and Masqud are put in charge of the conquered towns; Bala pursues Jalaldin Sultan and Qan Melig to the land of the Hindus, and Chinggis returns to the Tula. A note on the text: the Mongol is a Ming Chinese-character transcription, and the glosses in square brackets are the Ming glossators’ own; where the English departs from them or is unsure, the note says so.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.l: Jüchi, Cha’adai, Ögödei, three sons, Ürüngechi town having-made-enter,
sentences.i: Jüchi, Cha’adai and Ögödei, the three sons, took in the city of Ürüngechi,
sentences.n: Read this as one long sentence, broken here at its converbs: the three named sons are the subject, and the verb does not come until the third unit. Oroγ̇ulžu is oro- “enter” + the causative -γ̇ul- + the converb -žu (Ming 敎投入着, “making enter”); “took in” (made it come over to them) is my reading, as the glossary also records “making surrender” for this form. Ürüṅgeči is printed Örüṅgeči here and Ürüṅgeči later; the Ming 城名 says only “a town”.

sentences.i: and divided the towns and people among themselves, the three together,
sentences.n: γurbaγ̇ula is γurban “three” + the collective -γ̇ula, “the three all together” (Ming 三箇). Balaγad irgen “towns, people” are two plain nouns side by side, as the object.

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan-to share not brought-out.
sentences.i: but they gave Chinggis Qahan no share.
sentences.n: Qaγan-a is the dative-locative -a (Ming 行, “to”). Ese “not” (Ming 不曾) negates a past act, and the verb is γarγažuγ̇u: γarγa- “bring out” (γar- “go out” + causative; the stem is read from the Ming 出了) + the narrative past -žuγ̇u. So “did not bring out a share to the Qahan”.

sentences.l: unsubmitting those-who-were Sartaul people’s Sultan-(object) having-humbled, towns people his took we.
sentences.i: “The Sartaul people were unsubmissive; we humbled their Sultan and took his towns and people.
sentences.n: Öčen-melžen (Ming 不服, “not submitting”) is one word whose inside I cannot parse. Aγsad is a- “be” + the participle with plural -d, “those who were”, so the unsubmitting ones are the Sartaul. Doroiddaγ̇uižu is printed with -γ̇ui-, which is a slip for the causative -γ̇ul- “making bow down” (Ming 敎屈下着): the Han 兀勒 writes γul, not γui. It is the same verb as doroitaγ̇uluγsan-dur in U10; the stem doroida- (the glossary’s lemma for doroidaγ̇ulžu) is itself uncertain. An-u “his” (Ming 他的) comes after its nouns. Abuγ̇ai is ab- “take” + the final past -uγ̇ai; bida is “we” (Ming 咱, the inclusive form).

sentences.l: Dividing to-be-taken Ürüngechi town sharing-out those-who-take sons all Chinggis Qaγan’s are.
sentences.i: As for the city of Ürüngechi, which was to be taken by dividing: the sons who share it out and take it are all Chinggis Qahan’s own.
sentences.n: The hardest sentence of the speech. Abdaqu is ab- “take” + the passive -da- + the participle -qu, “to be taken” (Ming 被要的); abqun is ab- + -qun, “those who take” (Ming 要的每). The Ming glosses fit my reading, that the sons who divided Ürüngechi and took it are the Qahan’s men, but they give no verb linking the first half, so “which was to be taken by dividing” is uncertain. Qaγ̇an-uγ̇ai is a genitive-possessive (Ming 的; the ending is not certain) with bi “is”.

sentences.l: Heaven earth-to strength being-added, Sartaul people-(object) this-much when-humbled,
sentences.i: With strength added to us by Heaven and Earth, when we had humbled the Sartaul people thus far,
sentences.n: Nemegdežü is neme- “add” (Ming 添) + the passive -gde- + -žü, “being added”. Teṅgeri γažar-a “Heaven (and) earth” has its dative -a (Ming 行) on the second word only, shared by both. The formula “strength added by Heaven and Earth” returns in U29. Doroitaγ̇uluγsan-dur is the causative “humble” (doroida- + -γ̇ul-) + the participle -γsan + the dative-locative, “at the having-humbled”, that is “when (we) had humbled”. Edüi (Ming 這些) is “so much, thus far”.

sentences.l: we many men geldings your rejoicing maγaižu are.
sentences.i: we, your many men and horses, rejoice, and maγaižu.
sentences.n: Ba “we” (Ming 俺) heads the clause. Olon ere aγta is “many men, geldings”, that is men and horses (Ming 軍 馬). Čin-u “your” (Ming 你的) comes after the nouns, as in-ü and an-u do, and I read it with them, “your many men and horses”, not as “rejoicing in you”; bajasču is “rejoicing” (Ming 歡喜着). Maγaižu has no Ming gloss at all (the bracket is empty in the print) and I cannot parse it; I leave it unread rather than invent a sense.

sentences.t: Qaγan jakin ein kiliṅlažu amui.

morph.gloss: to be angry (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 怒) [怒着]

sentences.l: Qaγan why thus being-angry is.
sentences.i: Why, Qahan, are you so angry?
sentences.n: Qaγan has no case ending, so it is either an address (“Qahan, ...”) or a subject (“the Qahan is angry”); the Ming says only 皇帝. Since the three are reporting to him I take it as an address. Jakin (Ming 爲甚) is “why”, ein “thus”, and kiliṅlažu amui is “is being angry”, from a stem kiliṅla- inferred from the Ming 怒.

sentences.i: If you show them favour and let them into your presence, would that do?” So they reported.

sentences.n: Boro šibaγ̇un is “fledgling hawk” from the Ming 雛 鷹; boro usually means “grey”, but the Ming gloss decides it here. Bolija-dur (Ming 調習裏, “in the taming”) is a noun I do not otherwise know. Sai is glossed 恰纔 “just now” here, not the usual “good”. Oroqu metü is oro- “enter” + the participle -qu + metü “like”.

sentences.t: köġüd sai edüi ajalan surun büküi-dür

morph.gloss: just now (Ming 恰纔; elsewhere sai 'good') (adverb) [恰纔]
so much, only this much (adverb) [這些]
to go on campaign (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 征進) [征進]

sentences.l: sons just-now this-much campaigning learning, while-being,
sentences.i: while the sons are only now learning to campaign,
sentences.n: Ajalan (Ming 征進, “go on campaign”) is a stem ajala- inferred from the Ming + -n; surun is sur- “learn” + -un. The two converbs sit before büküi-dür “while being”, so “while learning to campaign”. Edüi again “only this much”.

sentences.t: köġüd-i šiṅtalun mene metü jakin ein doṅγodumu.

morph.gloss: back, behind (word uncertain, not parsed; from the Ming 退後) [退後]
repeatedly, troublesomely (word uncertain; from the Ming 頻煩) [頻︀煩]
to rebuke, blame (variant of doṅγod-; Ming 恠責) (verb) [恠責有]

sentences.l: sons-(object) back repeatedly like, why thus rebuking?
sentences.i: why rebuke them so, as if they were shrinking back time after time?
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Šiṅtalun (Ming 退後, “retreat, behind”) and mene (Ming 頻煩, “repeatedly, troublesomely”) are words I cannot parse; with metü “like” I read “as if (they) kept drawing back”. The sons carry the accusative again (Ming 行). Doṅγodumu is doṅγodu- “rebuke” (Ming 恠責有), the glossary’s doṅγodu- (a variant of doṅγod- in U18), + the present -mu.

sentences.t: Köġüd ajužu sedkil(i)-jen alγasaγ̇užai.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to grow slack, become lax (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 懈怠) [懈怠恐]
apprehensive: lest, for fear that (Ming 恐)

sentences.l: Sons fearing, own-heart lest-grow-slack.
sentences.i: The sons, afraid, may let their own hearts grow slack.
sentences.n: Sedkil(i)-jen is sedkil “heart” + the reflexive -(i)jen, “their own heart” (Ming 心 自的行); the (i) is Shiratori’s linking vowel. Alγasaγ̇užai “lest (they) grow slack” as in U15.

sentences.t: Naran šiṅgekü-eče urγuqu-da kürtele dain irgen bi.

morph.gloss: to set, fall (of the sun) (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 落處) [落處]

words.reading: 兀舌兒中忽中忽-荅 urγuqu-da

morph.gloss: to rise, come out (of the sun) (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 出處) [出處行]
terminal converb: until, as far as
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓]

sentences.l: Sun from-the-setting at-the-rising up-to, enemy people there-are.
sentences.i: From where the sun sets to where it rises there are enemy peoples.
sentences.n: Šiṅgekü-eče (Ming 落處, “place of falling”) and urγuqu-da (Ming 出處行, “place of coming out”) are participles with “from” and “at”; their stems šiṅge- “set” and urγu- “rise” are inferred from the Ming. With kürtele “as far as” they mark the whole span of the world.

sentences.t: Man-i Töbödüd nogod(i)-jan tukirču ileġesü

morph.gloss: we (exclusive; oblique stem man-) (first-person plural pronoun); also 'and' [俺行]
the Töbödüd (Ming 西番每 'Tibetans'; word uncertain; plural -d) (people name) [西番每]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form; (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to incite, urge on (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 唆) [唆着]

sentences.l: Us Töbödüd dogs-own inciting if-send,
sentences.i: If you send us, the Töbödüd, inciting your own dogs,
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Man-i is ba “we” (exclusive, Ming 俺) in its oblique stem man- + the accusative. Töbödüd the Ming glosses 西番每, “Tibetans”; I cannot fit it into the sentence (an apposition, “us, the Töbödüd”, is the least strained) and have left it as printed, in `i` too, as a people-name. Nogod(i)-jan is noγai “dog” + plural -d + the reflexive, “one’s own dogs” (Ming 狗每 自的行); tukirču is tukir- “incite” (Ming 唆) + -ču; ileġesü is ile- “send” + the conditional. The English “inciting your own dogs” keeps the words as they stand; a comparison (“as one sets one’s dogs on”) is a guess the text does not write.

sentences.t: dain irgen-i ba teṅgeri γažar-a küčü nemegdežü

morph.gloss: people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓 行]
we (exclusive; oblique stem man-) (first-person plural pronoun); also 'and' [俺]
to add (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 添) [被添着]

sentences.l: enemy people-(object), we, Heaven earth-to strength being-added,
sentences.i: with strength added to us by Heaven and Earth, as for the enemy peoples,
sentences.n: Dain irgen-i is the object of abčirasuγai in the next unit. Ba “we” again; nemegdežü as in U10, the same formula.

sentences.t: altan müṅgü aγ̇urasun tabar irgen orγan čima-da abčirasuγai.

morph.gloss: length of cloth (stem as printed; uncertain) (noun) [段匹]

households, folk (Ming 人煙 'smoke of people') (noun) [人煙]
you (second-person pronoun; oblique stem čima-) [你 行]

words.reading: 阿卜赤舌剌速中孩 abčirasuγai

morph.gloss: to bring along (ab- 'take' plus a second verb; uncertain) (verb) [將來咱]

sentences.l: gold silver cloth goods people households you-to let-us-bring.
sentences.i: we shall bring you gold and silver, cloth and goods, their people and households.
sentences.n: Abčirasuγai is abčira- “bring along” + the first-person optative -suγai (Ming 咱, “let us”); abčira- is ab- “take” plus a second verb, and its inside is uncertain. Čima-da is či “you” in the oblique stem čima- + the dative-locative. Orγan (Ming 人煙, “the smoke of people”) is households. Aγ̇urasun “length of cloth” is the printed spelling of a word I am not sure of.

sentences.t: Ali irgen keġeġesü ene höröne Baγtad irgen-ü Qaliba Soltan keġekü bi keġemüi.

morph.gloss: people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓]
west, to the west (Ming 西) (noun, adverb) [西]
the Baγtad, a people (Ming 種名) (people name) [種名]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓 的]
Qaliba, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
sultan, a title (Ming 王 'king') (noun, title) [王]
is, exists (verb; perhaps a short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: which people if-you-say, this west Baqtad people’s Qaliba Sultan that-called is, is-said.
sentences.i: If you say, ‘Which people?’ — in the west there is one called Qaliba, Sultan of the Baqtad people, it is said.
sentences.n: Ali (Ming 那箇) “which”; keġeġesü “if (you) say” (Ming 說呵). Ene höröne is “this west” (Ming 西; the Ming writes 俺, “we, our”, under ene, which I read as “this”). Baγtad irgen-ü is a genitive before Qaliba Soltan, “the Sultan of the Baγtad people”, and `i` keeps that link. Baγtad is glossed 種名 “a tribe”, Qaliba 人名 “a man”; the Ming gives only those labels and I keep to the text. Keġekü bi keġemüi is “the said one exists, is said”.

sentences.t: Teġün-dür ba ajalasuγai" keġen öčiġešü

morph.gloss: that (oblique stem of tere) (pronoun) [那的 行]
we (exclusive; oblique stem man-) (first-person plural pronoun); also 'and' [俺]
to go on campaign (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 征進) [征進咱]
to say to a superior, report (verb) [奏呵]

sentences.l: That-to we let-us-campaign" thus-saying, when-reported,
sentences.i: Let us march against them!” So they reported.
sentences.n: Teġün-dür (Ming 那的 行) is “to that”; ba “we”; ajalasuγai is ajala- + the optative -suγai, “let us campaign”. The closing quotation mark is printed at ajalasuγai”; the rest is as in U16.

sentences.t: Qaγan soγ̇oražu ede üġes-tür žaliražu

morph.gloss: to be appeased, relent (Ming 解釋 'explain, release'; stem uncertain) (verb) [解釋着]
to calm down, subside (of anger) (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 怒息) [怒息着]

sentences.l: Qaγan appeased, these words-at anger-calming,
sentences.i: The Qahan was appeased, and his anger subsided at these words,
sentences.n: Soγ̇oražu (Ming 解釋着, “explain, release”) I read as “being appeased”; the stem is uncertain. Üġes-tür is üge “word” + plural -s + the dative-locative, “at the words”. The name of the Qahan comes twice in a row (here and in U34); it is one man, and the second naming opens the main clause.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žöbšiježü žarliγ bolurun:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
to approve, agree to (verb; Ming 道是) [道是着]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan approving, decree when-issuing:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan agreed, and issued a decree:
sentences.n: Žöbšiježü is žöbšije- “approve, agree” (Ming 道是, “say it is so”) + -žü; žarliγ bolurun is “when making a decree”, rendered “issued a decree” as before. The decree opens in the next unit, where Shiratori prints the opening mark.

sentences.t: "Qoṅγai, Qoṅtaγar, Sormaqan γurban qorčin-i sojurγažu

morph.gloss: Qongqai, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [(人)名]
Qongtaqar, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
Sormaqan, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
quiver-bearers, archers (qor 'quiver' + agent -či + plural -n; uncertain) (noun) [帶弓箭的行]
to show favour, bestow a grace (verb) [恩賜着]

sentences.l: "Qongqai, Qongtaqar, Sormaqan three quiver-bearers-(object) showing-favour,
sentences.i: “Showing favour to the three quiver-bearers, Qongqai, Qongtaqar and Sormaqan,
sentences.n: The opening quotation mark is printed here; the closing mark comes at atuγai” in the next unit. Sojurγažu is sojurγa- “show favour” (Ming 恩賜着) + -žu. The sentence is not finished: I take it that favour is shown to the three, and the next unit says how.

sentences.t: Adargidai Qoṅγai, Doluṅgirdai Qoṅtaγar qojar-i min-u dergede atuγai"

morph.gloss: the Adargidai, a clan or people (Ming 種(名)) (name) [種(名)]
Qongqai, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [(人)名]
the Dolongirdai, a clan or people (Ming 種(名)) (name) [種(名)]
Qongtaqar, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
optative (third person): let it be, let them …

sentences.l: Adargidai Qongqai, Dolongirdai Qongtaqar two-(object) me-of near let-stay"
sentences.i: let Qongqai of the Adargidai and Qongtaqar of the Dolongirdai, those two, stay beside me.”
sentences.n: Adargidai and Doluṅgirdai are glossed 種(名), “a tribe”, and stand before the man’s name: “Qongqai of the Adargidai”. Qojar-i is “the two” with the accusative. Min-u “my” (Ming 我的) + dergede (Ming 根前, “beside”); atuγai is a- “be, stay” + the optative -tuγai, “let them stay”. The closing quotation mark is printed after atuγai.

sentences.t: Ötegedei Sormaqan-i Baγtad irgen-dür Qaliba Soltan-dur ajalaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: the Ötegedei, a clan or people (Ming 種名) (name) [種名]
Sormaqan, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名(行)]
the Baγtad, a people (Ming 種名) (people name) [種(名)]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓 行]
Qaliba, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
sultan, a title (Ming 王 'king') (noun, title) [王行]
to go on campaign (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 征進) [敎征進了]

sentences.l: Ötegedei Sormaqan-(object) Baqtad people-to Qaliba Sultan-to caused-to-campaign.
sentences.i: Sormaqan of the Ötegedei he sent to make war on the Baqtad people and Sultan Qaliba.
sentences.n: Ajalaγ̇ulba is ajala- + the causative -γ̇ul- + the past -ba (Ming 敎征進了, “had (him) campaign”). The datives (Ming 行) give “against”. Ötegedei is glossed 種名 “a tribe”, as the others in the decree. With this unit the section ends.

sentences.t: Basa Hindus irgen Baγtad irgen qojar-un žaγ̇ura

morph.gloss: the Hindus, a people (Ming 種) (people name) [種]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓]
the Baγtad, a people (Ming 種名) (people name) [種(名)]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓]
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)

sentences.l: Again Hindus people, Baqtad people two-of between,
sentences.i: Again, between the Hindus and the Baqtad people,
sentences.n: Hindus (Ming 種, “a tribe”) is a people name. Qojar-un is “of the two” and žaγ̇ura “between, in the middle” (Ming 其間), so the place is the space between the two peoples. The sentence goes on in the next two units.

sentences.t: Aru, Maru, Madasari irgen-ü Abtu balaγasun-dur

morph.gloss: Aru, a people (Ming 種(名)) (people name) [種(名)]

words.reading: 巴剌中合孫-突︀舌兒 balaγasun-dur

sentences.l: Aru, Maru, Madasari people’s Abtu city-in,
sentences.i: in the city of Abtu, which belongs to the Aru, Maru and Madasari peoples,
sentences.n: Aru, Maru and Madasari are each glossed 種(名), “a tribe”; the glossary also has aru “back”, but the Ming shows these are names. Abtu is glossed 城名, “a town”. Irgen-ü “of the people” ties the town to the three peoples.

sentences.t: Dörbetei Dörbe-Doγšin-i ajalaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: the Dörbetei, a clan or people (Ming 種(名)) (name) [種(名)]

words.reading: 朶舌兒伯-朶黑失泥 Dörbe-Doγšin-i

morph.gloss: Dörbe-Doqshin, a man's name (Ming (人名)) (personal name) [(人名)行]
to go on campaign (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 征進) [征進了]

sentences.l: Dörbetei Dörbe-Doqshin-(object) caused-to-campaign.
sentences.i: he sent Dorbai-Doqshin of the Dörbetei to campaign.
sentences.n: Dörbetei is glossed 種(名), “a tribe”; Dörbe-Doγšin-i is glossed (人名)行, “a man”, and is the object of ajalaγ̇ulba. Shiratori prints Dörbe-Doγšin here and Dorbai-Doγšin in §239, but the Han for the first half is the same (朶舌兒伯), so it is one man of the Dörbetei; `i` gives the form used in §239, Dorbai-Doqshin.

sentences.t: Basa Sübeġetei baγ̇atur-i ümegši

morph.gloss: Sübegetei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
hero, brave man (noun; Ming 勇士) [勇士行]
northward, to the north (Ming 迤北) (adverb; form uncertain) [迤北]

sentences.l: Again Sübegetei hero-(object), northward,
sentences.i: Again, Sübegetei the hero, to the north —
sentences.n: A long sentence in six units (U41 to U46); its verb is ajalaγ̇ulba in U46, and the name Sübegetei is repeated there to pick the thread up. Baγ̇atur (Ming 勇士, “brave man”) is a title after the name. Ümegši (Ming 迤北, “to the north”) I cannot analyse further.

sentences.l: Qanglin, Kibcha’ud, Bajigid, Orusud, Majarad, Asud, Sasud, Serkesüd, Keshimir, Bolar, Raral
sentences.i: the Qanglin, the Kibcha’ud, the Bajigid, the Orusud, the Majarad, the Asud, the Sasud, the Serkesüd, the Keshimir, the Bolar and the Raral,
sentences.n: Eleven names, each glossed 種(名), “a tribe”, and counted in the next unit. Some look familiar, but the text gives only the forms and I leave them as names.

sentences.t: ede harban nigen aimaγ qarin irgen-dür kürtele

morph.gloss: nation, state (Ming 邦; uncertain: the glossary has qarin 'back, again', Ming 囘, and 'tribe, division', Ming 部) (noun) [邦]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓 行]

sentences.i: as far as the peoples of these eleven tribes and nations,
sentences.n: Harban nigen is “ten one”, eleven. Aimaγ (Ming 部落) is “tribe”; qarin (Ming 邦) I read as “nation”, though elsewhere in the glossary it means “back” and, once, “division” (Ming 部); the sense here is uncertain, and the Ming 邦 is all I have to go on. Irgen-dür kürtele is “reaching to the people”, the pattern of dative + kür- + -tele.

sentences.t: Idil, Žajaγ usutan müred ketülün

Jajaq, a river (Ming 河名) (name) [河名]

sentences.i: crossing the water-rich rivers Idil and Jajaq,
sentences.n: Idil and Žajaγ are glossed 河名, “a river”. Usutan is usu “water” + -tan “having” (Ming 水有的每), “the water-having”, that is “full rivers”; müred is müren “river” + -d. Ketülün is ketül- “cross” + the converb -ün (the glossary writes it -n).

sentences.t: Kiwamen, Kermen balaγasun-dur kürtele

morph.gloss: Kiwamen, a town (Ming 城名) (name) [城名]
Kermen, a town (Ming 城名) (name) [城名]

words.reading: 巴剌中合孫-突︀舌兒 balaγasun-dur

sentences.l: Kiwamen, Kermen town-to as-far-as,
sentences.i: and as far as the cities of Kiwamen and Kermen,
sentences.n: Both names are glossed 城名, “a town”. Kürtele “until, as far as” here closes the journey.

sentences.t: Sübeġetei baγ̇atur-i ajalaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: Sübegetei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
hero, brave man (noun; Ming 勇士) [勇士行]
to go on campaign (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 征進) [敎征進了]

sentences.l: Sübegetei hero-(object) caused-to-campaign.
sentences.i: he sent Sübegetei the hero on campaign.
sentences.n: The verb at last. Ajalaγ̇ulba as in U37. No subject is printed; it is Chinggis, the subject of the decree-giving in the section before.

sentences.t: Basa Sartaγ̇ul irgen-i abun baražu

morph.gloss: the Sartaul, a people (the Ming 囘囘 'Muslims') (people name) [囘囘]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓 行]
to be finished, used up (verb) [了了着]

sentences.l: Again Sartaul people-(object) taking finishing,
sentences.i: Again, when he had finished taking the Sartaul people,
sentences.n: Abun baražu is ab- “take” + -un, bara- “be finished, used up” + -žu; the Ming 取 了了着 gives “having finished taking”.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan decree when-issuing:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: Shiratori prints an opening quotation mark at Balaγad in the next unit but no closing mark anywhere in the section. I close the decree after talbižu in `i`, because what follows is told in the third person and in the past tense; this is a doubtful reading, and the decree may run on.

sentences.t: "Balaγad balaγad-tur daruγačin talbižu

morph.gloss: towns, cities (plural of balaγasun “town”, in -d) (noun, plural) [城每]

words.reading: 巴剌中合惕-圖舌兒 balaγad-tur

morph.gloss: towns, cities (plural of balaγasun “town”, in -d) (noun, plural) [城每 裏]
dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form, after d)
governor, garrison commander (Ming 鎭守官名; stem daruγa-; formation uncertain) (noun) [鎭守官名]
to set down, leave in place (verb) [放着]

sentences.l: "Towns, towns-in governors leaving
sentences.i: “Leave a governor in each town.”
sentences.n: Balaγad balaγad-tur is “towns, in the towns”, a distributive. Daruγačin (Ming 鎭守官名, “a guard-post officer”) I render “governor”; talbižu is talbi- “set down, leave” + -žu, a converb that Shiratori leaves hanging; the imperative “Leave” in `i` is mine, the English of a decree that has no finite verb.

sentences.l: Ürüngechi town-from Jalawachi, Masqud named father sons two Qurumshi clan-having Sartaul coming,
sentences.i: From the city of Ürüngechi there came two Sartaul of the Qurumshi clan, father and son, named Jalawachi and Masqud,
sentences.n: Nere-ten is nere “name” + -ten “having” (Ming 名有的每), and oboγ-tan is oboγ “clan” + -tan (Ming 姓有的): “those having the name”, “having the clan”. Ečige köġüd qojar is “father, sons, two”; köġüd is plural in form, but Masqud is a single son, so I read “father and son”. Jalawači, Masqud and Qurumši are glossed 人名 / 姓(名).

sentences.n: Josu töre is a pair (Ming 道理 體例, “principle, regulation”); josu is a variant of josun, which is written josun in the same sentence. Ügüležü is ügüle- “speak” + -žü.

sentences.i: and it was said that they knew them in accord with what is right;
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Josun-dur adali is “like (in accord with) the right” (Ming 理行 相似), and kelelegdežü is kele- “speak” + the passive -gde- + -žü, “being spoken (of)” (Ming 被說着). The Ming glosses meden 知, “know”, here, whereas in the next units mede- is 管, “manage”. Who says it is not stated.

sentences.n: Köġüd-i is plural in form for a single son, as in U50 (Ming 兒子(每)行). In-ü “his” (Ming 他(的)) is set before the name. Qurumši-ji is the clan name with the accusative. Daruγas-luγ̇a is printed in two pieces, daruγas- and luγ̇a, and counted as two words: daruγa + plural -s + the comitative -luγ̇a (Ming 鎭守的(每) 一同), “together with the governors”. Bidan-u “our” (Ming 咱的) is the inclusive form.

sentences.i: and he took along his father Jalawachi and brought him to take charge of the Kitad capital, Zhongdu.
sentences.n: Žuṅdu is Shiratori’s reading; the Ming glosses the city 大都 (“great capital”), and I give the form as Zhongdu, as before. Kitad-un is “of the Kitad” (Ming 契丹), the realm of northern China. Abčiražü … abčiraba is “taking along … brought”, a pair of verbs on one stem. sentences.i: Because these two, Jalawachi and Masqud, out of the Sartaul men, were able in the rules and principles of a city,
sentences.n: Sartaγtai is glossed 囘囘, “Muslims”, as Sartaγ̇ul is, and is Sartaγ + -tai (I take it for the Sartaul); küġün-(n)eče is küġün “man” + the ablative, with the (n) Shiratori’s (Ming 人處). Čidaqu-jin is čida- “be able” + -qu + a genitive-like -jin (Ming 能的(的)); it is hard to say how it hangs, and the word order töre josun is the reverse of josu töre in U51. Tula (Ming 上頭) is “because of”.

sentences.l: seventh year, Hen year, autumn, Tula’s Black Forest-in, palaces-in, came-down.
sentences.i: In the seventh year, the Hen year, in autumn, he camped in his palace tents in the Black Forest of the Tula.
sentences.n: Dolodiγ̇ar is doloγ̇an “seven” + the ordinal -diγ̇ar (Ming 第七), the same seven as in U58; takija žil is “the Hen year”, in the twelve-year cycle. Tula-jin is “of the Tula” (Ming 河名 的), and qara tün “black forest” (Ming 黑 林). Ordos-tur is ordo + plural -s + the dative-locative (Ming 宮(每) 裏). Baγ̇uba is “came down”, here “camped”.
